name: Eliezer
source_summary: A prophet from Mareshah who pronounced the LORD's judgment on King Jehoshaphat of Judah for allying himself with the wicked King Ahaziah of Israel in a shipbuilding venture, a judgment fulfilled when the ships were wrecked.
family_friendly_summary: Eliezer was a prophet who lived in the town of Mareshah. King Jehoshaphat of Judah, normally a good and faithful king, made a mistake: he teamed up with King Ahaziah of Israel, who did not follow God, to build a fleet of trading ships. Eliezer spoke up and told Jehoshaphat that because he had partnered with someone who did wrong, God would not let the plan succeed. Sure enough, the ships were wrecked and never sailed. Eliezer's message reminded God's people that even good kings can get into trouble when they team up with the wrong partners.
adult_story: Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah appears once in Scripture, delivering a prophetic word of judgment to King Jehoshaphat of Judah (2 Chronicles 20:35-37). Late in an otherwise faithful reign, Jehoshaphat allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, described as one "who acted wickedly," to build a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber intended to sail to Tarshish for trade. Eliezer confronted the king directly: "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has destroyed your works." The prophecy was immediately vindicated -- the ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish (20:37). The episode echoes an earlier partnership between Jehoshaphat and Ahab, Ahaziah's father, which also drew prophetic rebuke (2 Chronicles 19:2), suggesting a recurring pattern in Jehoshaphat's reign: a generally godly king repeatedly tempted to compromise Judah's covenant faithfulness through alliances with Israel's idolatrous royal house. Eliezer's brief appearance stands alongside other minor prophets in Chronicles whose entire recorded ministry is a single confrontational message -- but one that Scripture records as accurate and consequential.
christ_connections: Eliezer's warning that partnership with wickedness undermines even a faithful king's work anticipates the New Testament's call to be "unequally yoked" with no other master, since only singular allegiance to Christ secures what believers build (2 Corinthians 6:14).
